import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reconstruction conjecture

The *deck* of a finite graph $G$ is the multiset of isomorphism classes of the vertex-deleted
subgraphs $G - v$, one *card* for each vertex $v$ of $G$. The reconstruction conjecture of Kelly
and Ulam says that a graph on at least three vertices is determined, up to isomorphism, by its
deck.

The analogous statement for digraphs is false (Stockmeyer). The new digraph reconstruction
conjecture of Ramachandran instead attaches to each card $D - v$ the degree pair
$(\deg^{+}(v), \deg^{-}(v))$ of the deleted vertex, and says that every finite digraph is
determined, up to isomorphism, by this degree-associated deck.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *New digraph reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_digraph_reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- P. J. Kelly, *A congruence theorem for trees*, Pacific J. Math. 7 (1957), 961–968.
- S. Ramachandran, *On a new digraph reconstruction conjecture*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B
  31 (1981), 143–149.
- P. K. Stockmeyer, *The falsity of the reconstruction conjecture for tournaments*,
  J. Graph Theory 1 (1977), 19–25.
- B. D. McKay, *Reconstruction of small graphs and digraphs*, Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022),
  [arXiv:2102.01942](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01942).
-/
namespace ReconstructionConjecture
variable {V W : Type*}

/- ## Graphs

A *card* of a graph `G` is a vertex-deleted subgraph `G.induce {v}ᶜ`. Two finite graphs have the
same deck (the same multiset of isomorphism classes of cards) exactly when there is a bijection
`σ` between their vertex sets with `G - v ≅ H - σ v` for every vertex `v`. This is the classical
definition of hypomorphic graphs, and we take it as the definition. -/

blocks.code:
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ)
blocks.docstring:
Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if there is a bijection `σ` between their
vertex sets such that the vertex-deleted subgraphs `G - v` and `H - σ v` are isomorphic for
every vertex `v` of `G`. For finite graphs this says exactly that `G` and `H` have the same deck,
i.e. the same multiset of isomorphism classes of vertex-deleted subgraphs.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.induce and SimpleGraph.Iso (≃g) in Mathlib, which are used as building blocks; there is no deck/hypomorphism predicate. A Multiset of isomorphism classes via SimpleGraph isoSetoid-style quotient was considered but rejected as needlessly heavy.
justification.name: ReconstructionConjecture.Hypomorphic
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of the deck of a graph or of hypomorphic graphs. Defined as ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ), the classical bijection definition equivalent (for finite graphs) to equality of decks as multisets of isomorphism classes.

blocks.name: Hypomorphic
blocks.text:
/--
Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if there is a bijection `σ` between their
vertex sets such that the vertex-deleted subgraphs `G - v` and `H - σ v` are isomorphic for
every vertex `v` of `G`. For finite graphs this says exactly that `G` and `H` have the same deck,
i.e. the same multiset of isomorphism classes of vertex-deleted subgraphs.
-/
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.of_iso {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} (φ : G ≃g H) :
    Hypomorphic G H :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_adj_iff⟩⟩⟩
blocks.name: Hypomorphic.of_iso
blocks.text:
/-- Isomorphic graphs are hypomorphic. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.of_iso {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} (φ : G ≃g H) :
    Hypomorphic G H :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_adj_iff⟩⟩⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.card_eq [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    (h : Hypomorphic G H) : Fintype.card V = Fintype.card W :=
  let ⟨σ, _⟩ := h
  Fintype.card_congr σ
blocks.docstring: Hypomorphic graphs have the same number of vertices.

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hypomorphic_bot_top_fin_two :
    Hypomorphic (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  ⟨Equiv.refl _, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.refl _, fun {a b} => by
    obtain rfl : a = b := by
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := a
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := b
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ha hb
      revert v a b
      decide
    simp⟩⟩⟩
blocks.docstring:
The two graphs on two vertices (the empty graph and the single edge) are hypomorphic. Together
with `not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two`, this is why the reconstruction conjecture assumes at
least three vertices.

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two :
    ¬ Nonempty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) ≃g (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2))) := by
  rintro ⟨f⟩
  have := f.map_adj_iff (v := 0) (w := 1)
  simp at this

theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) (hV : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hGH : Hypomorphic G H) : Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by

blocks.docstring:
**The reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly–Ulam):
any two hypomorphic finite simple graphs on at least three vertices are isomorphic.

That is, a finite simple graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its
deck, the multiset of isomorphism classes of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The hypothesis of at
least three vertices is needed because the two graphs on two vertices have the same deck. It is
only imposed on `G`, since hypomorphic graphs have the same number of vertices
(`Hypomorphic.card_eq`).

/- ## Digraphs

We use Mathlib's `Digraph`, whose adjacency relation is an arbitrary relation `Adj`. In the
digraph reconstruction problem, digraphs are loopless and have at most one arc for each ordered
pair of vertices (so arcs in both directions between two vertices are allowed); we impose
looplessness as a hypothesis. The vertex-deleted subdigraph `D - v` is the restriction
`Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v)` of `Adj` to the vertices other than `v`, and a digraph isomorphism is a
relation isomorphism `≃r` between adjacency relations. -/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def outDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard
blocks.docstring: The out-degree of the vertex `v` in the digraph `D`: the number of arcs leaving `v`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.degree (only for simple graphs, not Digraph); Digraph in Mathlib.Combinatorics.Digraph has no degree notion.
justification.name: ReconstructionConjecture.outDegree
justification.why_needed: Mathlib's Digraph has no degree API; out-degree of v is needed for the degree-associated deck. Defined as {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard.

theorem outDegree_top [Fintype V] (v : V) : outDegree (⊤ : Digraph V) v = Fintype.card V := by

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) (v : V) :
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (φ v) := by
  unfold outDegree
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ φ.injective]
  congr 1
  ext w
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := φ.surjective w
  simp [φ.map_rel_iff]
blocks.name: outDegree_relIso

blocks.code:
def DegreeHypomorphic (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v,
    Nonempty (Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) ≃r Subrel E.Adj (· ≠ σ v)) ∧
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (σ v) ∧ inDegree D v = inDegree E (σ v)
blocks.docstring:
Two digraphs `D` and `E` have the same **degree-associated deck** if there is a bijection `σ`
between their vertex sets such that, for every vertex `v` of `D`, the vertex-deleted subdigraphs
`D - v` and `E - σ v` are isomorphic and `v` and `σ v` have the same out-degree and the same
in-degree. For finite digraphs this says exactly that the multisets of degree-associated cards
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))`, with `D - v` taken up to isomorphism, coincide.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's Subrel and RelIso (used for cards and isomorphisms); FormalConjecturesForMathlib's Digraph.Hom in Combinatorics/Digraph/Tournament.lean (homomorphisms only, not isomorphisms or induced subdigraphs).
justification.name: ReconstructionConjecture.DegreeHypomorphic
justification.why_needed: Ramachandran's degree-associated deck (multiset of pairs (D − v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v)) up to isomorphism of the card) has no counterpart in Mathlib or the repo. Defined via a bijection σ : V ≃ W with Nonempty (Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) ≃r Subrel E.Adj (· ≠ σ v)) and equal out-/in-degrees for every v.

blocks.name: DegreeHypomorphic
blocks.text:
/--
Two digraphs `D` and `E` have the same **degree-associated deck** if there is a bijection `σ`
between their vertex sets such that, for every vertex `v` of `D`, the vertex-deleted subdigraphs
`D - v` and `E - σ v` are isomorphic and `v` and `σ v` have the same out-degree and the same
in-degree. For finite digraphs this says exactly that the multisets of degree-associated cards
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))`, with `D - v` taken up to isomorphism, coincide.
-/
def DegreeHypomorphic (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v,
    Nonempty (Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) ≃r Subrel E.Adj (· ≠ σ v)) ∧
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (σ v) ∧ inDegree D v = inDegree E (σ v)

theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.ii [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) (hD : ∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) (hE : ∀ w, ¬ E.Adj w w)

blocks.docstring:
**The new digraph reconstruction conjecture** (Ramachandran, 1981):
any two finite loopless digraphs with the same degree-associated deck are isomorphic.

That is, a finite digraph (no loops, at most one arc for each ordered pair of vertices, arcs in
both directions allowed) is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of pairs
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))` over its vertices `v`, where the card `D - v` is taken up to
isomorphism. No lower bound on the number of vertices is needed, since the degree pairs already
distinguish the digraphs on two vertices. The plain digraph analogue of the reconstruction
conjecture, without the degree pairs, is false (Stockmeyer).

-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.ii [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) (hD : ∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) (hE : ∀ w, ¬ E.Adj w w)
    (hDE : DegreeHypomorphic D E) : Nonempty (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) := by
  sorry
end ReconstructionConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Kelly–Ulam conjecture as made precise in the article: any two finite simple graphs on at least three vertices with the same deck (the MULTISET of isomorphism classes of single-vertex-deleted induced subgraphs) are isomorphic; the ≥3-vertex hypothesis is essential (both 2-vertex graphs share a deck), and the deck must be a multiset, not a set (the set version is Harary's separate, stronger conjecture, which the statement does not name).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the Kelly–Ulam conjecture identically in substance: finite simple graphs G : SimpleGraph V, H : SimpleGraph W with 3 ≤ Fintype.card V, hypothesis ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ), conclusion Nonempty (G ≃g H). For finite graphs this bijection formulation is exactly equality of the decks as MULTISETS of isomorphism classes (matching cards with multiplicity), so it is the Kelly–Ulam conjecture and not Harary's set version; the ≥3-vertex hypothesis is present (on G; H inherits it via the bijection, recorded as the API lemma Hypomorphic.card_eq). c01 chosen as base: named, documented `Hypomorphic` definition, proved API lemma (iso ⇒ hypomorphic) validating the definition, and a boundary-case test that ⊥ and ⊤ on Fin 2 are hypomorphic. I added c02's complementary test `not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two` so the necessity of the ≥3 hypothesis is checked in Lean. c05 (universe-restricted `Type`), c08 (wrong copyright header), c04/c07 (redundant/less polished) were mathematically fine but stylistically weaker.

claims.decomposer_note: Ramachandran's (1981) conjecture that every finite digraph (loopless, at most one arc per ordered pair, 2-cycles allowed) is determined up to isomorphism by its degree-associated deck, i.e. the multiset of pairs (D − v, (outdeg v, indeg v)) over its vertices; no minimum-order hypothesis is needed since the degree pairs already separate the 2-vertex digraphs, and it must NOT be formalized with the plain digraph deck, since that unweakened version is false (Stockmeyer's non-reconstructible tournaments), as the article notes.
claims.reviewer_why: All candidates state Ramachandran's conjecture with the degree-associated deck: finite Mathlib `Digraph`s (relation-valued, so at most one arc per ordered pair and 2-cycles allowed), looplessness imposed explicitly on both digraphs (∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v), hypothesis ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, (D − v ≅ E − σ v as RelIso of Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v)) ∧ outdeg v = outdeg (σ v) ∧ indeg v = indeg (σ v), conclusion Nonempty (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj), no minimum-order hypothesis. This is equality of the multiset of pairs (D − v, (od v, id v)) up to isomorphism of cards; the false plain-deck version is not stated. c01 chosen: uses Mathlib primitives (Subrel, RelIso) rather than a bespoke induce, has documented `outDegree`/`inDegree`/`DegreeHypomorphic`, and fully proved API lemmas (RelIso preserves degrees; iso ⇒ degree-hypomorphic) and tests (degrees in ⊤) validating that Set.ncard gives the right degrees on finite types. c01, c02, c03, c06 are equivalent; c04/c05/c07/c08 also equivalent but with weaker docs/style.

context: In graph theory, informally, the reconstruction conjecture says that graphs are determined uniquely by their subgraphs.  It is due to Kelly and Ulam.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table correctly identifies the two named conjectures, the multiset (not set) deck for slot i with the ≥3-vertex hypothesis, and the degree-associated deck (not the plain deck) for slot ii. The Wikipedia entry's phrase 'whether a graph is uniquely determined by its vertex-deleted subgraphs' is a question in form but names conjectures with positive assertions, so both slots are stated as plain propositions rather than with answer(sorry), following the repository's convention for conjectures.

/-!
# Reconstruction conjecture

The *deck* of a finite graph $G$ is the multiset of isomorphism classes of the vertex-deleted
subgraphs $G - v$, one *card* for each vertex $v$ of $G$. The reconstruction conjecture of Kelly
and Ulam says that a graph on at least three vertices is determined, up to isomorphism, by its
deck.

The analogous statement for digraphs is false (Stockmeyer). The new digraph reconstruction
conjecture of Ramachandran instead attaches to each card $D - v$ the degree pair
$(\deg^{+}(v), \deg^{-}(v))$ of the deleted vertex, and says that every finite digraph is
determined, up to isomorphism, by this degree-associated deck.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *New digraph reconstruction conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_digraph_reconstruction_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- P. J. Kelly, *A congruence theorem for trees*, Pacific J. Math. 7 (1957), 961–968.
- S. Ramachandran, *On a new digraph reconstruction conjecture*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B
  31 (1981), 143–149.
- P. K. Stockmeyer, *The falsity of the reconstruction conjecture for tournaments*,
  J. Graph Theory 1 (1977), 19–25.
- B. D. McKay, *Reconstruction of small graphs and digraphs*, Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022),
  [arXiv:2102.01942](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01942).
-/

namespace ReconstructionConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/- ## Graphs

A *card* of a graph `G` is a vertex-deleted subgraph `G.induce {v}ᶜ`. Two finite graphs have the
same deck (the same multiset of isomorphism classes of cards) exactly when there is a bijection
`σ` between their vertex sets with `G - v ≅ H - σ v` for every vertex `v`. This is the classical
definition of hypomorphic graphs, and we take it as the definition. -/

/--
Two simple graphs `G` and `H` are **hypomorphic** if there is a bijection `σ` between their
vertex sets such that the vertex-deleted subgraphs `G - v` and `H - σ v` are isomorphic for
every vertex `v` of `G`. For finite graphs this says exactly that `G` and `H` have the same deck,
i.e. the same multiset of isomorphism classes of vertex-deleted subgraphs.
-/
def Hypomorphic (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v, Nonempty (G.induce {v}ᶜ ≃g H.induce {σ v}ᶜ)

/-- Isomorphic graphs are hypomorphic. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.of_iso {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W} (φ : G ≃g H) :
    Hypomorphic G H :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_adj_iff⟩⟩⟩

/-- Hypomorphic graphs have the same number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem Hypomorphic.card_eq [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    (h : Hypomorphic G H) : Fintype.card V = Fintype.card W :=
  let ⟨σ, _⟩ := h
  Fintype.card_congr σ

/--
The two graphs on two vertices (the empty graph and the single edge) are hypomorphic. Together
with `not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two`, this is why the reconstruction conjecture assumes at
least three vertices.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem hypomorphic_bot_top_fin_two :
    Hypomorphic (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  ⟨Equiv.refl _, fun v => ⟨⟨Equiv.refl _, fun {a b} => by
    obtain rfl : a = b := by
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := a
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := b
      simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ha hb
      revert v a b
      decide
    simp⟩⟩⟩

/-- The two graphs on two vertices are not isomorphic. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_nonempty_iso_bot_top_fin_two :
    ¬ Nonempty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) ≃g (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2))) := by
  rintro ⟨f⟩
  have := f.map_adj_iff (v := 0) (w := 1)
  simp at this

/--
**The reconstruction conjecture** (Kelly–Ulam):
any two hypomorphic finite simple graphs on at least three vertices are isomorphic.

That is, a finite simple graph on at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its
deck, the multiset of isomorphism classes of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The hypothesis of at
least three vertices is needed because the two graphs on two vertices have the same deck. It is
only imposed on `G`, since hypomorphic graphs have the same number of vertices
(`Hypomorphic.card_eq`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.i [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) (hV : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hGH : Hypomorphic G H) : Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  sorry

/- ## Digraphs

We use Mathlib's `Digraph`, whose adjacency relation is an arbitrary relation `Adj`. In the
digraph reconstruction problem, digraphs are loopless and have at most one arc for each ordered
pair of vertices (so arcs in both directions between two vertices are allowed); we impose
looplessness as a hypothesis. The vertex-deleted subdigraph `D - v` is the restriction
`Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v)` of `Adj` to the vertices other than `v`, and a digraph isomorphism is a
relation isomorphism `≃r` between adjacency relations. -/

/-- The out-degree of the vertex `v` in the digraph `D`: the number of arcs leaving `v`. -/
noncomputable def outDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj v w}.ncard

/-- The in-degree of the vertex `v` in the digraph `D`: the number of arcs entering `v`. -/
noncomputable def inDegree (D : Digraph V) (v : V) : ℕ :=
  {w | D.Adj w v}.ncard

/-- In the complete digraph every vertex has out-degree equal to the number of vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_top [Fintype V] (v : V) : outDegree (⊤ : Digraph V) v = Fintype.card V := by
  simp [outDegree, Set.ncard_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]

/-- In the complete digraph every vertex has in-degree equal to the number of vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem inDegree_top [Fintype V] (v : V) : inDegree (⊤ : Digraph V) v = Fintype.card V := by
  simp [inDegree, Set.ncard_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]

/-- Digraph isomorphisms preserve out-degrees. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem outDegree_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) (v : V) :
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (φ v) := by
  unfold outDegree
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ φ.injective]
  congr 1
  ext w
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := φ.surjective w
  simp [φ.map_rel_iff]

/-- Digraph isomorphisms preserve in-degrees. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem inDegree_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) (v : V) :
    inDegree D v = inDegree E (φ v) := by
  unfold inDegree
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ φ.injective]
  congr 1
  ext w
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := φ.surjective w
  simp [φ.map_rel_iff]

/--
Two digraphs `D` and `E` have the same **degree-associated deck** if there is a bijection `σ`
between their vertex sets such that, for every vertex `v` of `D`, the vertex-deleted subdigraphs
`D - v` and `E - σ v` are isomorphic and `v` and `σ v` have the same out-degree and the same
in-degree. For finite digraphs this says exactly that the multisets of degree-associated cards
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))`, with `D - v` taken up to isomorphism, coincide.
-/
def DegreeHypomorphic (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) : Prop :=
  ∃ σ : V ≃ W, ∀ v,
    Nonempty (Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) ≃r Subrel E.Adj (· ≠ σ v)) ∧
    outDegree D v = outDegree E (σ v) ∧ inDegree D v = inDegree E (σ v)

/-- Isomorphic digraphs have the same degree-associated deck. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem DegreeHypomorphic.of_relIso {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W} (φ : D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) :
    DegreeHypomorphic D E :=
  ⟨φ.toEquiv, fun v => ⟨⟨⟨φ.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv fun a => by simp, φ.map_rel_iff⟩⟩,
    outDegree_relIso φ v, inDegree_relIso φ v⟩⟩

/-- Digraphs with the same degree-associated deck have the same number of vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem DegreeHypomorphic.card_eq [Fintype V] [Fintype W] {D : Digraph V} {E : Digraph W}
    (h : DegreeHypomorphic D E) : Fintype.card V = Fintype.card W :=
  let ⟨σ, _⟩ := h
  Fintype.card_congr σ

/--
**The new digraph reconstruction conjecture** (Ramachandran, 1981):
any two finite loopless digraphs with the same degree-associated deck are isomorphic.

That is, a finite digraph (no loops, at most one arc for each ordered pair of vertices, arcs in
both directions allowed) is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of pairs
`(D - v, (deg⁺ v, deg⁻ v))` over its vertices `v`, where the card `D - v` is taken up to
isomorphism. No lower bound on the number of vertices is needed, since the degree pairs already
distinguish the digraphs on two vertices. The plain digraph analogue of the reconstruction
conjecture, without the degree pairs, is false (Stockmeyer).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reconstruction_conjecture.parts.ii [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (D : Digraph V) (E : Digraph W) (hD : ∀ v, ¬ D.Adj v v) (hE : ∀ w, ¬ E.Adj w w)
    (hDE : DegreeHypomorphic D E) : Nonempty (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj) := by
  sorry

end ReconstructionConjecture

items: Deck equality is formalized via the classical hypomorphism bijection (∃ σ : V ≃ W with G − v ≅ H − σ v for all v) rather than by literally building a Multiset of isomorphism classes. For finite graphs this is equivalent to equality of the multisets of isomorphism classes of cards (a bijection matches cards with multiplicity), so the multiset (Kelly–Ulam) version is captured, not Harary's set version. Building a literal Multiset of isomorphism classes would require transporting all cards to a common vertex type or quotienting a universe of graphs, which adds complexity without changing the mathematical content.
The minimum-order hypothesis for slot i is stated as 3 ≤ Fintype.card V only; card W = card V follows from the bijection σ inside Hypomorphic (recorded as the API lemma Hypomorphic.card_eq).
Finiteness is expressed with [Fintype V] [Fintype W]; the conjecture is false for infinite graphs (the article gives counterexamples), so restricting to finite vertex types is essential and faithful.

For slot ii, Mathlib's Digraph allows loops, so looplessness is imposed as explicit hypotheses on both digraphs (Ramachandran's digraphs are loopless with at most one arc per ordered pair; 2-cycles are allowed, and Digraph allows them). Mathlib's Digraph has at most one arc per ordered pair by construction.

Vertex-deleted subdigraphs are expressed with Mathlib's Subrel D.Adj (· ≠ v) (the restriction of the adjacency relation to vertices ≠ v), and digraph isomorphism is Mathlib's RelIso on adjacency relations (D.Adj ≃r E.Adj); this avoids bespoke Digraph.induce/Digraph.Iso definitions. SimpleGraph.Iso is itself a RelIso, so the two slots use the same notion of isomorphism.

Out-degree and in-degree are defined as Set.ncard of the out-/in-neighbour sets. Under the [Fintype V] hypothesis of the conjecture these are the true degrees; ncard's junk value 0 on infinite sets is never reached in the statement.

No lower bound on the number of vertices is imposed in slot ii, following Ramachandran (the degree pairs separate the two-vertex digraphs). Digraphs with 0 or 1 vertex are trivially reconstructible, so including them is harmless and faithful.

Only the two slots in the decomposition table are stated as research-open theorems; Harary's set-reconstruction and edge-reconstruction conjectures, which the list entry does not name, are deliberately not included. API/test lemmas (isomorphic ⇒ (degree-)hypomorphic, equal vertex counts, the two-vertex graphs are hypomorphic, degrees in the complete digraph) are included with full proofs to validate the bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Original list entry is terse; both slots were formalized per the decomposition notes and the Wikipedia articles (Kelly–Ulam multiset deck with ≥3 vertices; Ramachandran's degree-associated deck for loopless digraphs with no minimum order). No candidate omitted a slot and no omission reasons needed weighing. Modeling choice common to all candidates and adopted: deck equality is expressed as a hypomorphism bijection σ : V ≃ W with cardwise isomorphisms rather than a literal Multiset of a quotient type; for finite vertex types this is provably equivalent to multiset equality of isomorphism classes and avoids cross-universe quotients. Only 3 ≤ card V is imposed in slot i (card W = card V follows from σ; API lemma Hypomorphic.card_eq records this). Digraph looplessness is an explicit hypothesis on both digraphs since Mathlib's Digraph allows loops. Bespoke definitions (Hypomorphic, outDegree, inDegree, DegreeHypomorphic) are kept in the problem file namespace; a maintainer may prefer moving outDegree/inDegree to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/Digraph/. Final file compiles with only the two 'declaration uses sorry' warnings; the only >100-char lines are reference URLs in the module docstring, as is common in the repo.
